claim.title: Bias is non-increasing with more samples
claim.statement: For n<=d, the bias B_n=||E_X[Proj_{X^perp}(beta)]||^2 is non-increasing in n; i.e., B_{n+1} <= B_n.
claim.test_plan: Fix d=1000 and ||beta||_2=1. For each n in a dense grid from 1 to d-1 (e.g., every 10 samples), generate many independent X matrices, compute Proj_{X^perp}(beta), and estimate B_n=||E[Proj_{X^perp}(beta)]||^2 by Monte Carlo. Plot B_n versus n.
claim.evidence_in_paper: Equation (3) and the sentence: 'From Equation 3, the bias is non-increasing with samples (B_{n+1} <= B_n), since an additional sample can only grow the rowspace.'
claim.success_criterion: The estimated sequence B_n is non-increasing in n (allowing small Monte Carlo deviations): B_{n+1} <= B_n + 0.01||beta||^2 for all sampled n, with no systematic increasing trend.
